Useful comparison, but weaker geographic/social fit than European/British references.

candidates.reason: The actual medium doorway/recoil frame communicates withdrawal and fear far more convincingly than the primitive pose. Movement remains mainly rigid/whole-body rather than fully articulated.

decisions.why_selected_or_pending: Prefer VICTOR-POSE-D for the medium recoil language; keep final approval blocked by source/costume/provenance requirements.
decisions.remaining_risk: Need final costume-time decision and clean source file.

candidates.reason: Bespoke proportional human figure built from literary constraints, Bell surface/action anatomy, skeletal/anatomical references, and period engraving language. Best research direction so far because it preserves proportion/beauty while allowing uncanny surface treatment; must still survive the actual shot.

Uses von Holst's early Frankenstein silhouette/proportion language as the dominant visual reference. Strong period identity and story connection, but a single historical illustration may overconstrain anatomy and angles; needs comparison against a more anatomy-driven bespoke design.
Excellent anatomy evidence but poor final creature asset: too clinical, not story-specific, and would make the film look like an imported anatomy plate. Retain only as design/reference evidence.

Actual creation/recoil shot tests materially outperform the primitive body: proportionate human anatomy, flowing hair/drapery and engraved surface quality read correctly at wide/medium scale. Flat asset supports restrained breathing/lift only; independent limb convulsion remains unresolved. Generated-asset rights/provenance require final confirmation before approval.

decisions.why_selected_or_pending: Prefer CBODY-D for the current visual direction at wide/medium scale. Do not mark final until a clean individual source and required articulation/rights gates pass.
decisions.remaining_risk: Independent limb convulsion, clean final source file and final rights review remain open.

candidates.reason: Start from a proportionate, potentially beautiful human head and create horror through pallor, sockets, lips, eye treatment, shadow and animation rather than arbitrary cranial deformation.
Builds the head/profile language from the 1831 frontispiece. Strong Frankenstein identity and engraving fit, but must be checked against source-contract choice and close-up anatomy.

Blockheaded/scarred/deformed monster shorthand is rejected because it is generic, later-iconography driven, and conflicts with the source idea of proportionate limbs/features originally selected as beautiful.

First-eye close-up reads as a proportionate human head made uncanny by complexion, socket, hair, shadow and animation rather than generic monster deformation. Passed close-up and eye-reveal motion tests.

decisions.why_selected_or_pending: Prefer CHEAD-D for current lookdev. It is visually stronger than primitive and generic-grotesque directions, but remains provisional pending clean final source/provenance.
decisions.remaining_risk: Final alpha/source cleanup and continuity with the final full-body asset remain open.

candidates.reason: Long lustrous black hair treated as several flowing engraved masses that break the silhouette and partially obscure the face.
More individual flowing locks with restrained rim light. Could read more human and beautiful before becoming uncanny, but may be expensive/noisy at video resolution.
Hair acts as a nearly solid black curtain with a few flowing cuts, maximizing silhouette clarity and hiding facial information. Risk: may lose the 'lustrous' quality.

decisions.why_selected_or_pending: All three remain viable until tested at medium and close-up scales.
decisions.remaining_risk: Need continuity across body shot and eye close-up without adding excessive line noise.

candidates.reason: A dull yellow/watery eye with low luminance contrast, pale socket and subtle wet specular detail. Horror comes from life appearing in something almost dead, not from neon emission.
Keeps most of the eye in engraving shadow and reveals only a small dull-yellow iris/scleral plane. Strong style integration, but may become unreadable in the macro shot.
Rejected despite visual punch: it turns the eye into a modern sci-fi/electrical trope and directly weakens the dull-yellow/watery source description.

Uses the real engraved eye and a JavaScript occlusion mask for closed->partial->open states. Avoids the rejected electric-blue-glow trope and preserves a dull yellow/watery reading. Passed start/mid/end motion frames after alpha-compositing fix.

decisions.why_selected_or_pending: Prefer CEYE-D. Final approval waits for clean individual source/provenance and continuity with the final Creature head.
decisions.remaining_risk: Rights/provenance and final head continuity are unresolved.

candidates.reason: Sequence: hard breath/chest expansion -> distal finger/hand spasm -> asymmetric convulsive limb motion -> incomplete head/torso rise. Closely maps source event order while remaining cinematic.
One stronger whole-body convulsion followed by unnerving stillness, then a small head/eye movement. Less literal breathing emphasis but potentially stronger horror rhythm.
Rejected because it imports a generic undead movement vocabulary and ignores the described hard breathing and convulsive first movement.

decisions.why_selected_or_pending: Create short motion tests for A and B with identical framing/audio before selection.
decisions.remaining_risk: Movement can become melodramatic or mechanically rigged; Bell-informed muscle/joint behavior must survive stylization.

candidates.reason: Reads clearly and is bespoke, but geometry/context should be refined against the museum record and contemporary galvanism source.
Authoritative object record and period-form reconstruction; geometry can inform our own asset without pasting museum imagery.
Best period experimental visual vocabulary; particularly useful for contextualizing the fictional laboratory.

Macro shot gains substantially more engraved material/construction detail than the primitive pile. Interaction is now handled by a separate JS contact lever rather than forcing a contaminated hand asset.

decisions.why_selected_or_pending: Prefer PILE-D for the macro visual direction, pending final-source/provenance and historical construction review.
decisions.remaining_risk: Generated source/provenance and exact functional reconstruction still need final validation.

candidates.reason: Recognisable period form, but construction details should be refined before final approval.
Surviving early-19th-century object gives precise materials/construction; standard museum raster remains reference-only for commercial output.
Strengthens period galvanism context and house-style integration.
The engraved jar integrates visually with the pile and passes the macro shot readability gate. Final historical construction details remain to be checked.

decisions.why_selected_or_pending: Prefer JAR-D for current macro lookdev, but retain museum-based direction as the factual validation source.
decisions.remaining_risk: Final functional/historical and generated-source rights review remain open.

candidates.reason: Recognisable period form, but construction details should be refined before final approval.
Surviving early-19th-century object gives precise materials/construction; standard museum raster remains reference-only for commercial output.
Strengthens period galvanism context and house-style integration.

decisions.why_selected_or_pending: Redraw/adjust the jar after construction-detail comparison; do not use the museum raster image under its standard noncommercial image licence.
decisions.remaining_risk: Final geometry and shot fit still unapproved.

candidates.reason: The hand candidate was removed after failing isolation/shot fit. A simple brass lever/contact built in JS is more controllable, visually clean and functionally legible; it closes over time and directly anchors the electrical arc.

decisions.why_selected_or_pending: Prefer CONTACT-D over the weak hand-driven interaction. Final historical geometry still needs factual review, but the shot mechanism itself passes.
decisions.remaining_risk: Historical contact geometry is interpretive and should not be overclaimed as canonical apparatus.

candidates.reason: Synthesize the 1800 city-view silhouette with university-site architecture evidence and the literary steeple cue. Strongest research direction because no single source has to do every job.
Stay very close to the 1800 copper engraving's city massing/roofline. Strong historical specificity but may be compositionally weak or too literal for the dramatic camera.

Emphasize the university/Hohe Schule identity over the whole city. Could better connect Victor to place, but available visual evidence spans different dates and must not be treated as an exact 1800 snapshot.
Rendered control candidate. It works compositionally but communicates generic old-European/Gothic city rather than Ingolstadt.

decisions.why_selected_or_pending: Render A, B and C as matched exterior approval frames using the same camera, storm and palette. Candidate A is the strongest research hypothesis, but it is not selected until the actual shot proves it.
decisions.remaining_risk: Historic evidence must be synthesized without false precision; steeple/site identity must read at 720p without turning the shot into an architectural diagram.

candidates.reason: Create a fictional laboratory building that belongs plausibly to the Ingolstadt/university urban fabric rather than falsely claiming Victor used a known exact building.
Using Hohe Schule geometry gives immediate university identity, but risks falsely implying that the novel specifies Victor's exact laboratory there.
Rejected because atmosphere alone is not location/story specificity.

decisions.why_selected_or_pending: Candidate A currently best satisfies story/location plausibility without inventing a false exact-site claim. It still needs a matched shot test against B.
decisions.remaining_risk: Need enough architectural specificity to feel Ingolstadt while preserving fictional latitude and cinematic silhouette.
